topic: Screened investing: which companies pass, and what it does to a portfolio

assumptions.notes: No euro figures. Screening has two layers: business activity (conventional banking and insurance, alcohol, gambling, pork products, adult entertainment typically excluded; many screens add tobacco and weapons) and financing (a widely used threshold of around one third for interest bearing debt and for cash and interest bearing securities relative to company size, and around 5% for prohibited income; exact ratios differ between standards). Purification: the prohibited portion of dividends is commonly given to charity. Sukuk replace bonds. Not religious guidance or investment advice.

beats.narration: A share is part ownership of a business, with profit and loss shared. That is why shares are generally considered permissible.
The first screen is what the company does. Conventional banking and insurance, alcohol, gambling and pork products are typically excluded.
The second is financing. Common tests cap interest bearing debt and cash at about a third, and prohibited income at about five percent.
Where a permitted company earns a little prohibited income, investors commonly give that share of dividends to charity. That is purification.
beats.subtext: That share of dividends, to charity

beats.narration: Screening changes the portfolio. Fewer banks and insurers, more technology and healthcare, and a shorter list of companies.
beats.subtext: Sometimes ahead of the market, sometimes behind

beats.narration: Bonds pay interest, so they are out. The closest replacement is the sukuk: a share in an asset and the income it produces.
So the two layer screen asks: what the company does, its debt, its cash, its prohibited income, and what gets purified.

caption.instagram:
Investing in shares can fit an interest free plan. The hard part is which companies.

A share is part ownership of a business, with profit and loss shared, which is why shares are generally considered permissible. Screening has two layers. What the company does: conventional banking and insurance, alcohol, gambling and pork products are typically excluded. How it is financed: common tests cap interest bearing debt and cash at about a third each, and prohibited income at about 5%, though exact ratios differ between standards. A small prohibited share of dividends is commonly given to charity. The result tilts away from banks and insurers, and sukuk take the place of bonds, so a screened portfolio will not move in step with the headline index.

The two layer screen: what the company does, its debt, its cash, its prohibited income, and purification.
